 Through:- Mrs. Monika Kohli, Sr. AAG  Ms. Pallavi Sharma, Assisting counsel to  Mr. Ravinder Gupta, AAG Coram:
 HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE VINOD CHATTERJI KOUL, JUDGE  JUDGMENT 1.

Through the medium of the instant petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India,
petitioner prays for quashing of Order No. CLA/ACR/Rsi/18-19/364-366 dated 25.01.2019 passed by respondent No.2 and to command the respondents to pay compensation to the petitioner as per the award dated 03.10.2015 for the land falling under Khasra No.210 measuring 03 Kanals, and no.
213 min measuring 03 Kanals and 10 Marlas of village Gajore, Tehsil Pouni, District Reasi, which has been taken over by WP(C) 3475/2019 them along with interest @ 12% p.a.

Further a direction is Onkar Singh S/O Lt Sh. Mansa Ram R/O vs State Of J&K Through Its on 6 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118953035/
1 also sought to be passed upon respondent No.2 to deposit the entire amount with the Registry of this Court along with interest @ 12% from the date of taking possession of his land i.e., 2009.

sentences.text: 2. Petitioner states that his land has been acquired by the respondent No.2 at the instance of respondent No. 3 on 03.10.2015, but no compensation has been paid till date, despite the direction passed by this Court in writ petition, being OWP No. 360/2017, on 20.03.2017.
It is stated that after the contempt proceedings were initiated against the respondent No.2 by this Court, he without going into the facts of the case, passed the order impugned dated 25.01.2019.

3. Petitioner further states that respondent No.3 has constructed a road from Village Khera Lehar to Gajore under PMGSY phase VII after the land under the occupation of the petitioner comprising of Kh. No. 210 measuring 03 kanals & Kh. No.213 min measuring 03 kanals and 10 marlas of Village Gajore, Tehsil Pouni, District Reasi, was acquired under Land Acquisition Act by respondent No.2 vide his award dated 03.10.2015.

It is stated that the acquaintance roll as obtained under the Right to Information Act also bears a testimony to this fact that petitioner is entitled to compensation as assessed by the respondent No.2 for the land taken out of his possession for construction of road.
However, till date the petitioner has not been paid compensation, despite approaching number of times for release of the same.

It is stated that this Court vide order dated 01.04.2017 passed in OWP N. 360/2017 directed the respondent No. 2 to verify from the records as regards subject matter of the writ petition and do the needful for WP(C) 3475/2019 release of an amount of compensation in favour of the petitioner strictly in terms of the award dated 03.10.2015.
However, needful was not done, as such, petitioner was constrained to file contempt petition for non-compliance of the order before this Court.
The respondent No. 2 instead of complying with the order, passed the order impugned dated 25.01.2019.

4. Respondents 1 and 2 in their objections have resisted and controverted the contentions raised and grounds urged in the petition, inter alia, on the premise that pursuant to the filing of the contempt petition being CPOWP 136/2017, the respondents considered the claim of the petitioner in compliance to order dated 20.03.2017 and passed consideration order, whereby the claim of the petitioner was found without any merit and claim of the petitioner rejected vide order impugned dated 25.01.2019.

It is being further contended in the objections that the entry of the petitioner in the revenue record is only of 'Gair Maroosi tenant' which does not entitle him to any right to receive compensation for the acquired land.

5. Respondent no.3 has also filed objections, stating therein that the revenue department after verification of the record petitioner stands recorded as non-occupancy (Gair Maroosi) tenant which has come within the alignment of the road from Kherlehar to Gajore under Khasra No. 210 min measuring 3 kanals and khasra No. 213 min measuring 3 kanals in the village Gajore Tehsil Pouni.

It is stated that the PMGSY released an amount of Rs. 20.94 lacs in favour of the Collector Land Acquisition (Assistant Commissioner Revenue), Reasi, which was to be disbursed by him after the verification to the rightful claimants.
No compensation has been withheld by the respondents and the respondent No.3 has to release the same in favour of the petitioner in accordance with law.

2 6.

Respondent No.2-Collector Land Acquisition (Assistant Commissioner Revenue), Reasi, while rejecting petitioner's claim vide order impugned dated 25.01.2019 has held that petitioner is not entitled to compensation under the provisions of Circular instructions issued Vide Rev.LB-10/80 dated 23.02.2019 as father of the petitioner late Mansa Ram stands recorded as non-occupancy tenant (Gair Marusi).
7.

Learned counsel for the petitioner in support of his contention has relied upon a judgment of Division Bench of this Court in Krishana vs. State of J&K and Others, 2022 (2) JKJ [HC] 377, and also a judgment passed by a Coordinate Bench of this Court in case titled as Nisar Hussain & Ors vs.
State of J&K and ors. 2003 (3) JK[HC]228.
7.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text:

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the material on the file.
8. The only issue which arises for consideration in the instant matter is whether the petitioner is entitled to any compensation as per the aforesaid award.

9. The petitioner claims compensation on the basis of acquaintance roll as obtained under the Right to Information Act, which bears a testimony to the fact he is in cultivating possession as per Khasra Girdawari Rabi since 2016 and in the revenue record he has been show as Gair Muroosi.

10. In Banarsi Dass (through his L.Rs) and ors vs. Babu Ram, 1999(2) CLJ (HP), the High Court of Himachal Pradesh held that it is well settled law that in order to see whether there was relationship of tenant and landlord between the parties what has to be seen in the revenue records is WP(C)
3475/2019 not merely the column of possession/cultivation but also the column of rent.

entities.text: Banarsi Dass (through his L.Rs) and ors vs. Babu Ram, 1999(2) CLJ (HP)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was held that in the absence of any rent being paid, the person recorded merely as a tenant-at-will in the column of possession/cultivation does not become a tenant under the revenue law.

11. The Punjab and Haryana High Court in Ram Karan Vs. The Financial Commissioner and others 1980 P.L.J 295 held that it is well settled law that generally in the revenue record, the persons even in unauthorized possession are described as Gair Marusi Tenants in the column of cultivation, but from this entry alone, it cannot be held that the status of such persons is that of tenants unless in the rent column it is disclosed that such persons were liable to pay rent.

entities.text: Ram Karan Vs. The Financial Commissioner and others 1980 P.L.J 295
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
12. The acquaintance roll obtained by the petitioner under the Right to Information Act also bears a testimony to the fact that he is in cultivating possession of the Khasra Nos. 210 and 213 as per khasra Girdawari Rabi 2016 as 'Gair Murusi'.
13.

The Punjab & Haryana High Court in case titled Ram Kishan and others vs. Jagdish and others,
decided on 23.02.2018 (RSA 4412 of 2014), while describing literal meaning of Gair Marusi has held as follows:-
"As noticed earlier, the meaning of word Gair Marusi is non- occupancy.

entities.text: Ram Kishan and others vs. Jagdish and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of these entries, the plaintiffs are not even proved to be tenant on the land.
The word Gair Marusi itself does not imply that the person in occupation is a tenant.

For arriving at conclusion whether a person is tenant or Onkar Singh S/O Lt Sh. Mansa Ram R/O vs State Of J&K Through Its on 6 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118953035/
3 not, the entry in the column of rent has to be carefully read in conjunction with the entry in cultivation column.

entities.text: Onkar Singh S/O Lt Sh. Mansa Ram R/O vs State Of J&K
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the present case, the entry in the rent column does not show that the plaintiffs were in possession as a tenant under the land owners."

The judgments relied upon by the learned counsel for the petitioner does not support the claim of the petitioner, as in Krishana's case (supra) the petitioner was in possession of the State land since 1998- 1999 and had applied for conferring ownership rights to the competent authority and on the directions of the Deputy Commissioner, he had deposited the requisite fee of Rs.1085/- for the conferment of the ownership rights, whereas in Nissar Hussain's case (supra) while considering the question of compensation payable for the land in question acquired by the respondents, the Collector had apportioned the amount of compensation amongst the petitioners and private respondents therein who were the tenants under the petitioner and recorded, as such, in the revenue records.

The petitioners challenged the award to the extent it was relating to the payment of compensation to the private respondents and sought a direction for payment of the entire compensation being the owners of the land on the ground that prospective owner has absolutely no right to any compensation under law.

In the said case, this Court held that petitioners being the original owners along shall have the right to receive compensation for the land acquired and it was further directed that if compensation assessed for the land owned by the petitioners and held by the private respondents as tillers has been paid to them, the State Government shall be at liberty to recover the same.
15. In the present case, petitioner is seeking compensation of the land in question on the basis of an entry in the Khasra Girdawari Rabi 2016 recorded as "Gair Marusi".
Nothing has been placed on record to show that petitioner has applied for conferment of ownership rights for the land in question to the competent authority.
The instant petition is found to be without any merit and is, accordingly, dismissed.
(VINOD CHATTERJI KOUL) JUDGE Jammu 06.05.2024 Bir Whether approved for reporting?
